question_text: Who signs bills to become laws?

why_it_matters.text: After Congress passes a bill, it isn't law yet — the President has to sign it. That signature is the final step that turns the idea Congress agreed on into a rule everyone in America has to follow.

fun_fact.text: Signing a major bill is often a ceremony. President Lyndon Johnson used more than 75 pens to sign the Civil Rights Act of 1964 — and gave every pen away as a gift. One of the first went to Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
